claims.text: Bulk HfNbTaTiZr can be synthesized through powder-metallurgy routes.
The modeled bulk HfNbTaTiZr specimen has a measured oxygen impurity level of approximately 1 wt.%.
Ab initio calculations, actively learned moment-tensor potentials, and a Bayesian workflow can be integrated into one predictive framework.
Bayesian machine-learning corrections can account specifically for oxygen-related defects in HfNbTaTiZr.
The integrated framework can predict both thermal and electrical conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Oxygen occupies defect sites and produces local lattice distortions, grain-boundary modifications, or local bonding variations in the alloy.
Oxygen-induced structural changes alter phonon-scattering pathways in HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen-induced structural changes alter electron-scattering pathways in HfNbTaTiZr.
Oxygen impurities introduce localized disruptions and defect states that modify lattice vibrations and electronic scattering events.
Explicitly incorporating oxygen-defect effects will improve conductivity predictions relative to perfect-crystal analytical models.
The integrated model will achieve less than approximately 10% conductivity discrepancy from experiment over 0–200 K.
The integrated model will achieve less than approximately 10% conductivity discrepancy from experiment over 300–1200 K.
Conventional analytical conductivity models for this material assume perfect, defect-free crystals.
Conventional analytical models can have conductivity prediction errors greater than 20% for HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
The integrated model will outperform conventional analytical approaches in both specified temperature regimes.
The model's asserted applicability is limited to approximately 1 wt.% oxygen and the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K ranges.
Applicability outside the specified oxygen level or temperature ranges is unvalidated.
Four-probe electrical measurements and laser-flash thermal measurements can provide experimental conductivity benchmarks for the model comparison.
